content.headline: OpenAI’s claimed science breakthroughs spark a fight over access and scrutiny
content.shortHeadline: Researchers challenge OpenAI’s approach to sharing AI findings
content.standfirst: OpenAI says its models produced results in mathematics, computing and physics, but researchers say selected “shepherds” should not control who sees the work. The claims remain under examination, and some materials have not been fully released.

sources.originalTitle: OpenAI announces three big science discoveries and a new way to work with academics
Researchers are getting tired of OpenAI gatekeeping its breakthroughs

segments.body: OpenAI says its models have produced results in three fields, including a proposed refutation of the widely held Exponential Time Hypothesis. It has released some materials and assigned outside experts to guide how others are shared. The company’s announcement describes these as discoveries; they have not all been independently verified in the reporting.

segments.title: Who gets to check the work?
segments.body: Researchers interviewed by The Verge welcomed outside expertise but criticised restricting early access to people selected by OpenAI. The company’s mathematics advisory group has also warned that hand-picked access can create unequal access and borrowed authority, and urged open release of research outputs. OpenAI says it is experimenting with different approaches and acknowledges trade-offs.

perspectives.body: Several researchers quoted by The Verge say that public claims of breakthroughs should be accompanied by materials that everyone can scrutinise. They also argue that difficult-to-read proofs and selection of a small review group can make verification less open.

content.headline: AI bots made most responses to a UK consultation on disposable vapes
content.shortHeadline: AI bots flooded a UK consultation on disposable vapes
content.standfirst: Researchers say 90,835 of 118,756 responses to a 2023 government consultation were automated and opposed the proposed ban. Officials identified and excluded them, but researchers warn future campaigns may be harder to detect.

sources.originalTitle: AI bots flooded 2023 UK government consultation on disposable vapes ban

segments.body: A study published in Tobacco Control says 76% of responses to a UK consultation on the tobacco and vapes bill were machine-generated. The Department of Health and Social Care identified 90,835 automated submissions among 118,756 responses, almost all answering the same question in opposition to the proposed disposable-vape ban.

segments.title: A challenge for public consultation
segments.body: The department excluded the automated responses from its decision-making, and the ban later became law. Researchers say the episode appears to be the first documented large-scale automated attempt to interfere in a formal UK public-health consultation. They warn that better screening is needed, while recognising that barriers against bots can also make it harder for real people to participate.

content.headline: Real photos of storm damage were dismissed online as AI-generated
content.shortHeadline: Real storm photos were wrongly dismissed as AI fakes
content.standfirst: After a wall collapsed near Whitby Abbey, online commenters called eyewitness Sue Taylor’s unedited photographs fake. Independent images and witnesses backed her account, highlighting how genuine evidence can be doubted as AI-generated media spreads.

sources.originalTitle: These Storm Boelo images were not AI - but some people thought they were

segments.body: Sue Taylor posted photographs of stones from a collapsed wall lying on cars near Whitby Abbey after Storm Boelo. Dozens of commenters said the images were generated or altered with AI. The BBC says it reviewed independently posted images and video of the same damage and spoke to eyewitnesses who corroborated Taylor’s pictures.

segments.title: Scepticism needs evidence
segments.body: AI expert Theocharis Kyriacou said unusual-looking images are not necessarily artificial and that independent footage and eyewitness accounts matter more than first impressions. He warned that generative AI is eroding trust in photographs. He also urged people to distinguish healthy scepticism from automatically rejecting images that seem extraordinary.

content.headline: Amazon could be the biggest winner from Anthropic’s planned IPO
content.shortHeadline: Amazon stands to gain most from Anthropic’s planned IPO
content.standfirst: Anthropic’s convertible notes could become a large shareholding as the AI company prepares to go public. Amazon is also set to earn from a major cloud-spending commitment, illustrating how a supplier can benefit from a company it also backs.

sources.originalTitle: VCs will make billions on Anthropic’s IPO, but Amazon is set to make much (much) more

segments.body: Anthropic’s filing says Amazon holds convertible notes with $6.2bn in principal outstanding as of 30 June. Amazon’s filings valued those notes at $97.9bn, reflecting the rise in Anthropic’s valuation. The notes could convert into shares after an IPO, subject to a cap that Amazon may waive.

segments.title: Investor and supplier
segments.body: Amazon has also invested in preferred stock and is due to earn revenue under Anthropic’s commitment to spend at least $110bn on AWS over 10 years. Google, another major investor and cloud provider, also stands to benefit from its relationship with Anthropic. The filing warns that cloud providers can also be competitors, leaving potential conflicts of interest.

content.headline: Fleetwood knock Arsenal out of the Carabao Cup in a stunning shootout win
content.shortHeadline: Fleetwood stun Arsenal to reach Carabao Cup quarter-finals
content.standfirst: League Two Fleetwood held the Premier League champions to a 1-1 draw before winning on penalties. Arsenal’s 16-year-old Max Dowman was sent off late on, adding a further twist to a remarkable cup upset.

image.caption: Conor Haughey celebrates after scoring the penalty that sent Fleetwood into the quarter-finals.

sources.originalTitle: Dowman sees red as Arsenal dumped out, but did Arteta go too far?
'Biggest night in the club's history' for fearless Fleetwood

segments.body: Fleetwood Town have reached the Carabao Cup quarter-finals for the first time after eliminating Arsenal on penalties. Aaron Loupalo-Bi put the hosts ahead, Viktor Gyökeres equalised after the break, and the League Two side held on through normal time despite Arsenal dominating possession and attempts.

segments.title: A night to remember in Fleetwood
segments.body: Arsenal were reduced to 10 men when Dowman was sent off late in the match after reacting to a challenge. Goalkeeper Jay Lynch saved penalties from Ben White, Martin Ødegaard and Bruno Guimarães; Conor Haughey then scored the decisive kick. Fleetwood manager Matt Lawlor called it the club’s biggest night.

perspectives.body: Fleetwood left-back Jake Batty said the team’s league form had been below expectations, but cup football had brought out a different spirit. He hoped the excitement would carry into their next league game.

segments.title: Questions over Arteta’s reaction
segments.body: Manager Mikel Arteta looked angry as Dowman left the pitch and said the team had already discussed the need to control emotions. Paul Merson argued Arteta should have put an arm around the 16-year-old; former Everton midfielder Leon Osman called Dowman’s response poor and said he hoped the teenager learned from it.

content.headline: Abhishek Sharma’s 113 powers India to a record-breaking T20 chase of New Zealand
content.shortHeadline: Abhishek’s 113 leads India to a stunning T20 chase
content.standfirst: India reached 199 in just 13.2 overs in Wellington, with Abhishek Sharma making 113 from 38 balls. The six-wicket win gives India an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series.

sources.originalTitle: Abhishek hits 35-ball ton as India hammer New Zealand

segments.body: Abhishek Sharma hit 113 from 38 balls as India chased New Zealand’s 198-3 in 13.2 overs to win the third T20 by six wickets. He struck nine fours and 11 sixes, with 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi contributing 45 from 19 balls in an opening stand of 133.

segments.title: Series won with two matches left
segments.body: India’s 118 runs in the powerplay set a new record for international T20s, and the result gives them a 3-0 lead in the five-match series. Daryl Mitchell had earlier made 89 from 52 balls for New Zealand, but India reached the target with 40 balls to spare.

content.headline: Manchester United keep Michael Carrick in charge for Chelsea trip
content.shortHeadline: Man Utd stick with Carrick for Chelsea trip
content.standfirst: After considering his position following successive heavy defeats, United have decided their head coach will lead the team at Chelsea. The club has set no timetable for a further decision as it tries to steady a turbulent situation.

image.caption: Michael Carrick acknowledges supporters after Manchester United’s defeat by Bournemouth.

sources.originalTitle: Man Utd stick with Carrick - inside a turbulent 48 hours at Old Trafford

segments.body: Michael Carrick will remain Manchester United head coach for Saturday’s trip to Chelsea. The decision followed discussions at the club after defeats by Como and Bournemouth, with United 16th in the table. Carrick had said after the Bournemouth loss that he was carrying on as normal, without assuming what would happen next.

segments.title: No timetable for what comes next
segments.body: United have not set a deadline for reviewing Carrick’s position. The report says senior figures also believe the players must take responsibility for underperforming, while the club’s leadership has faced scrutiny. A decision after the international break is described as an obvious point to reassess, not a confirmed plan.

content.headline: England eliminated from ODI tri-series after Sri Lanka beat Pakistan
content.shortHeadline: England out of ODI tri-series after Sri Lanka win
content.standfirst: Sri Lanka’s eight-wicket victory in Lahore ended England’s hopes of reaching Saturday’s final. England have lost all three matches and will play Sri Lanka on Thursday in a match that can no longer affect qualification.

sources.originalTitle: England out of tri-series after Sri Lanka beat Pakistan

segments.body: England are out of the 50-over tri-series in Pakistan after Sri Lanka bowled the hosts out for 110 and chased the target in 18.1 overs. England needed Pakistan to win to keep their own route to Saturday’s final open; Sri Lanka’s eight-wicket victory closed it.

segments.title: A setback after a stronger year
segments.body: The exit follows three defeats, including losses after England were well placed chasing 303 and after failing to defend 430 against Sri Lanka. England had built momentum with ODI wins earlier in 2026, making this tournament a setback ahead of their scheduled Australia tour in November.

content.headline: Stuart Broad calls Lancashire’s treatment of James Anderson ‘disrespectful’
content.shortHeadline: Broad criticises Lancashire over Anderson decision
content.standfirst: Broad says Lancashire should have given Anderson a better send-off after deciding not to renew his contract. Anderson has not announced his retirement, and other counties are understood to be interested.

image.caption: Stuart Broad and James Anderson, England’s long-time bowling partners.

sources.originalTitle: Lancs treatment of Anderson 'disrespectful' - Broad

segments.body: Stuart Broad has criticised Lancashire’s handling of James Anderson’s departure, calling it “pretty disrespectful” and saying the county should have given the England great a better send-off. Lancashire has decided not to renew Anderson’s contract after he took 50 County Championship wickets last season.

segments.title: Anderson’s next step is unclear
segments.body: Broad said he believed Anderson still had a great deal to offer and that counties had already made contact. Anderson has expressed sadness at Lancashire’s decision but has not announced his retirement; Lancashire has said it will look into arranging a farewell.

content.headline: Starc’s late burst lifts Australia after Cummins chooses to bowl
content.shortHeadline: Starc’s late burst lifts Australia in Cape Town decider
content.standfirst: Australia dismissed South Africa for 329 on the first day of the series decider after a difficult opening session. Mitchell Starc took six wickets, including four in the closing overs, but the result remains undecided.

sources.originalTitle: Australia fight back to keep Cummins out of unwanted club... for now

segments.body: Australia fought back to bowl South Africa out for 329 on day one in Cape Town. After South Africa reached 203-1, Australia took regular wickets in the afternoon, then Mitchell Starc struck four times in the late spell to finish with 6-72.

segments.title: The toss decision remains in focus
segments.body: Pat Cummins chose to bowl after winning the toss, saying there was moisture in the pitch. The report notes that South Africa made 140 in the first session and that the late recovery does not, by itself, prove the decision was right. Australia’s batting response and the match outcome are still to come.

content.headline: Derek McInnes says he feels ‘guilt’ over leaving Hearts for Rangers
content.shortHeadline: McInnes accepts Hearts fans’ anger over Rangers move
content.standfirst: The Rangers manager is preparing to return to Tynecastle for the first time since leaving Hearts in the summer. He understands why supporters may react badly, despite his pride in what he achieved in Edinburgh.

image.caption: Derek McInnes, who is returning to Tynecastle as Rangers manager.

sources.originalTitle: McInnes admits 'guilt' over Hearts exit for Rangers

segments.body: Derek McInnes says he feels “guilt” about leaving Hearts for Rangers and accepts he may receive a hostile reception when he returns to Tynecastle. Hearts came close to winning the title under him last season, losing to Celtic on the final day.

segments.title: Pride in his time at Hearts
segments.body: McInnes said he loved his time at Hearts and was proud of what the team achieved, but understood supporters could feel let down by his move to Ibrox. He also described Hearts as title contenders under their new head coach, Wouter Vrancken.
